title: Confidence Gating — Escalate Only When Unsure

questions.prompt: A decision model reports a confidence of 0.9 on almost every input, including ones it gets wrong. What do you do first?
options: Check the model's accuracy in each score bucket against known answers
Switch to a different model immediately
questions.explanation: A score with no calibration is a number, not a measurement, so the first move is to see whether the score tracks correctness. Raising the threshold is tempting but pointless until you know what the score means — you'd just be moving a meaningless line.

questions.prompt: Your gate sends 90% of decisions to the frontier model. What is the most likely cause?
options: The decision model is too weak
The threshold is too high or was never calibrated
You need a larger context window
questions.explanation: A gate that escalates almost everything is usually mis-set, not outmatched. The fix is calibrating the score and moving the threshold. 'The model is too weak' is tempting, but even a strong decider escalates constantly if the line is drawn above most of its scores.

questions.prompt: You are gating a payments-routing loop. Which error should the threshold bias against?
options: False accepts — let more wrong decisions through
False escalates — bias toward escalating when unsure
Neither; the threshold does not change errors
Disable the gate and always use the biggest model
questions.explanation: When a wrong decision is expensive, bias the threshold low so uncertainty escalates rather than ships. 'Always use the biggest model' is tempting for the same reason, but it deletes the gate entirely and pays the strong path on every call — including the easy ones the gate existed to save.

questions.prompt: Why measure on a held-out slice after choosing a threshold?
options: To catch a threshold tuned to the specific examples you used
questions.explanation: If you pick T by staring at a set, T can fit that set's noise and fail on new inputs. A held-out slice measures generalization. The tempting answer treats it as a formality, but it is the only check that the threshold is real.
